## The question

[How to use MathJax library on Google App Engine](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4624154/how-to-use-mathjax-library-on-google-app-engine), asked by [systempuntoout](https://stackoverflow.com/users/130929/systempuntoout) on Stack Overflow (2011-01-07; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I'm trying to add Tex support to my application and I would like to use [MathJax][q-1] to render Mathematics formulas client side since I gave up the 
> server side solution explained [here][q-2].   
> The MathJax library is pretty fat (30.000 files) and it can't be easily installed on App Engine due to the [files number limitation][q-3].
>
> I have no experience with MathJax library so I'm open to other strategies like:  
>
>   - Available MathJax CDN
>   - Cutting down some directories/files to reduce the package's files number.
>
> Do you know any way to use Mathjax on Google App Engine?
>
>
>   [q-1]: http://www.mathjax.org/
>   [q-2]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4592501/tex-markup-how-to-render-it-in-html-with-python
>   [q-3]: http://code.google.com/intl/it-IT/appengine/docs/python/runtime.html#Quotas_and_Limits
:::

Since March 2011 [MathJAX has its own CDN][1], so you can now use it without uploading any files to GAE.  Just make sure this is in any page's header:

```python
<script type="text/javascript" async
  src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/mathjax/2.7.0/MathJax.js?...">
</script>
```

  [1]: http://docs.mathjax.org/en/latest/start.html
